In the event of any termination of this Agreement pursuant to Section 14.2, then, if SFJ has not caused a Program Transfer to occur pursuant to Section 3.20:"},{"id":"p0783","text":"14.3.1 to the extent not previously assigned to PB pursuant to Section 11.1.1.4, SFJ shall, and it hereby does, assign sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein to PB, such assignment to be effective in accordance with Section 11.1.1.4;"},{"id":"p0784","text":"14.3.2 effective as of such termination, SFJ shall, and it hereby does, assign to PB all of SFJ's and its Affiliates' right, title and interest in and to all Product Filings then owned or Controlled by SFJ or any of its Affiliates; provided that if any such Product Filing is not immediately transferable in a country, SFJ shall provide PB with all benefit of such Product Filing and such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB to timely transfer such Product Filing to PB or its designee or, at PB's option, to enable PB to obtain a substitute for such Product Filing without disruption to PB's development or Commercialization of the Product in the SFJ Territory;"},{"id":"p0785","text":"14.3.3 within [***] after assignment of the Product Filings pursuant to Section 14.3.2, SFJ shall deliver to PB: (a) true, correct and complete copies of all Product Filings in such country (in each case, whether held in the name of SFJ or any of its Affiliates),"},{"id":"p0786","text":"and disclose to PB in writing all previously-undisclosed Research Results within the Trial Data Package; (b) formally transfer or assign, or cause to be formally transferred or assigned, into the name of PB or its designee all Product Filings in such country (in each case, whether held in the name of SFJ or any of its Affiliates); and (c) take such other actions and execute such other instruments, assignments and documents as may be necessary to effect, evidence, register and record the transfer, assignment or other conveyance of such rights to PB or its designee;"},{"id":"p0787","text":"14.3.4 at PB's written request and election in PB's sole discretion, SFJ shall and hereby does, and shall cause its Affiliates to either:"},{"id":"p0788","text":"(i) wind down in accordance with Applicable Law and observing applicable ethical and regulatory guidelines any or all Clinical Trials being conducted by or on behalf of SFJ or its Affiliate as of the effective date of termination, at SFJ's cost and expense; or (ii) (x) transfer control to PB of any or all Clinical Trials being conducted by or on behalf of SFJ or its Affiliate as of the effective date of termination and (y) continue to conduct such Clinical Trials being conducted by or on behalf of SFJ or an Affiliate as of the effective date of termination for up to [***] to enable such transfer to be completed without interruption of any such Clinical Trial, in each case ((x) and (y)), at PB's cost and expense; and"},{"id":"p0789","text":"14.3.5 SFJ shall, and shall cause its Affiliates to, promptly assign to PB or its designee any and all Clinical Trial Agreements, CRO Agreements and other Vendor Agreements to which any of them is a party and cooperate in good faith with PB to provide appropriate notice and new contact information to the applicable Sites, Clinical Investigators, CROs and other Vendors and PB shall accept such assignment of all obligations of SFJ and its Affiliates thereunder without recourse to SFJ other than any indemnification obligations which SFJ may be liable for thereunder."},{"id":"p0790","text":"14.4 Surviving Obligations."},{"id":"p0791","text":"14.4.1 Accrued Rights and Obligations. Except as expressly set forth in Sections 3.20 and 14.4.2, and, if applicable, the Program Transfer Agreement, expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason will not release either Party from any obligation or liability which, at the time of such expiration or termination, has already accrued to the other Party or which is attributable to a period prior to such expiration or termination."},{"id":"p0792","text":"14.4.2 Exclusive Remedy. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, termination of this Agreement by a Party will be without prejudice to other remedies such Party may have at law or equity; provided that the payment by PB to SFJ of the amounts specified as being payable upon a given termination in Section 14.2 shall be in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have arising out of or in connection with the circumstances that formed the basis for such termination.."},{"id":"p0793","text":"14.4.3 Surviving Obligations. The following provisions of this Agreement, together with any other provisions that expressly specify that they survive, will survive expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement:"},{"id":"p0794","text":"14.4.3.1 ARTICLE 1, ARTICLE 9, ARTICLE 10, ARTICLE 11, ARTICLE 12, Section 13.1, Section 13.6, Section 14.4 and ARTICLE 15; and"},{"id":"p0795","text":"14.4.3.2 solely in the case of termination of this Agreement after payment by SFJ to PB of the Initial Development Cost Payment on the Initial Funding Date, but not in the case of expiration of this Agreement, Sections 3.20, 6.1- 6.7, 7.1-7.7 (in the case of such Sections 7.1-7.7, such provisions shall terminate only after all PB Obligations, other than contingent indemnity obligations, have been paid to SFJ or otherwise satisfied in accordance with this Agreement in full), 14.2 and 14.3."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ RECORDS","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0623","text":"RECORDS"},{"id":"p0624","text":"9.1 Accounting. Each Party will maintain materially complete and accurate accounting records related to this Agreement in accordance with GAAP. Each Party will retain such records for [***] after the earlier of expiration or early termination of this Agreement."},{"id":"p0625","text":"9.2 Clinical Trials-Related Records. Each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates and its and their Permitted Third Parties conducting Development of the Product to, maintain, in good scientific manner, complete and accurate books and records pertaining to Development of the Product hereunder, in sufficient detail to verify compliance with its obligations under this Agreement. Such books and records shall (a) be appropriate for patent and regulatory purposes, (b) be in compliance with Applicable Law, (c) properly reflect all work done and results achieved in the performance of its Development activities hereunder, and (d) be retained by such Party for such period as may be required by Applicable Law."}]}

{"sectionRef":"§ CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION","paragraphs":[{"id":"p0627","text":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION"},{"id":"p0628","text":"10.1 Confidentiality. Except to the extent expressly authorized by this Agreement or otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties (including, if applicable, in the Program Transfer Agreement), each Party (each, a \"Receiving Party\") agrees that, during the Term and for the [***] period following the expiration or termination of this Agreement (except that the obligations will survive thereafter with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under Applicable Law) or such longer periods for which such Confidential Information may be maintained pursuant to ARTICLE 9, it will keep confidential and will not publish or otherwise disclose and will not use for any purpose other than as provided for in this Agreement or, if applicable, the Program Transfer Agreement (which includes the exercise of any rights or the performance of any obligations hereunder or thereunder) any Confidential Information furnished to it by or on behalf of the other Party (each, a \"Disclosing Party\") or its Affiliates in connection with this Agreement or, if applicable, the Program Transfer Agreement. The foregoing obligations will not apply to any portion of such information or materials that the Receiving Party can demonstrate:"},{"id":"p0629","text":"10.1.1 was publicly disclosed by the Disclosing Party before or after such Confidential Information becomes known to the Receiving Party;"},{"id":"p0630","text":"10.1.2 was already known to the Receiving Party or any of its Affiliates, other than under an obligation of confidentiality or non-use, prior to when it was received from the Disclosing Party;"},{"id":"p0631","text":"10.1.3 is subsequently disclosed to the Receiving Party or any of its Affiliates by a Third Party lawfully in possession thereof without obligation to keep such Confidential Information confidential;"},{"id":"p0632","text":"10.1.4 has been published by a Third Party or otherwise enters the public domain through no fault of the Receiving Party or any of its Affiliates in breach of this Agreement; or"},{"id":"p0633","text":"10.1.5 has been independently developed by the Receiving Party or any of its Affiliates, without the aid, application or use of any Confidential Information of the other Party."},{"id":"p0634","text":"10.2 Authorized Disclosure. Each Party may disclose Confidential Information belonging to the other Party to the extent such disclosure is reasonably necessary for complying with Applicable Laws, including regulations promulgated by securities exchanges, provided that the Party required to disclose such information promptly notifies the Disclosing Party prior to making any such disclosure and cooperates with the Disclosing Party's efforts to seek confidential treatment or to otherwise limit disclosure."},{"id":"p0635","text":"Each Receiving Party may disclose the other Party's Confidential Information to its Affiliates, employees, agents, advisors, and independent contractors (including Permitted Third Parties) engaged by such Receiving Party, in each case (a) only to the extent such Persons need to know the Confidential Information solely in connection with the performance of this Agreement or, if applicable, the Program Transfer Agreement and (b) provided that each Person receiving Confidential Information must be bound by obligations of confidentiality and non-use at least as stringent as an equivalent in scope to those set forth in this ARTICLE 10 prior to any such disclosure and the Party making such disclosure to such Person shall be liable to the other Party for any breach of such obligations by such disclosee."},{"id":"p0636","text":"PB may disclose SFJ Confidential Information to MedImmune as necessary to comply with PB's obligations or exercise PB's rights under the AZ License (it being understood that any such disclosure will be made under the terms of Article 6 of the AZ License and that PB shall not be required to enter into any further confidentiality agreement with MedImmune for such purpose)."},{"id":"p0637","text":"Each Party may also disclose the material terms of this Agreement (including the form of Program Transfer Agreement) or provide a copy of this Agreement or a summary of such Party's findings during its due diligence investigation of the Products (if applicable) to any bona fide potential or actual investor, investment banker, acquirer, provider of debt or royalty financing, or other potential or actual financial partner without consent of the other Party, and provided that in connection with such disclosure, each disclosee must be bound by obligations of confidentiality and non-use at least as stringent as an equivalent in scope to those set forth in this ARTICLE 10 prior to any such disclosure and the Party making such disclosure to such disclosee shall be liable to the other Party for any breach of such obligations by such disclosee."},{"id":"p0638","text":"Notwithstanding anything in the foregoing to the contrary, Exhibit D constitutes PB's Confidential Information and not SFJ's Confidential Information, and PB may disclose Exhibit D to Third Parties as determined by PB in its sole discretion. In any event, each Party agrees to"},{"id":"p0639","text":"take all reasonable action to avoid unauthorized use or disclosure of Confidential Information of the other Party hereunder."},{"id":"p0640","text":"10.3 Return of Confidential Information. Except as otherwise provided herein, upon expiration or earlier termination of this Agreement, all Confidential Information (including any copies thereof) in written or other tangible form will, at the Disclosing Party's direction, be returned to the Disclosing Party or destroyed by the Receiving Party, and any Person(s) to whom the Receiving Party disclosed (with such destruction being certified in writing by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party), except (i) to the extent such Confidential Information is necessary to exercise any license and/or rights hereunder that survive such expiration or earlier termination; and (ii) one (1) copy of each document may be retained by the Receiving Party solely to the extent necessary to permit it to comply with any ongoing rights and responsibilities with respect to such Confidential Information."},{"id":"p0641","text":"10.4 MedImmune Confidential Information. With respect to any Confidential Information of PB that constitutes MedImmune Confidential Information, SFJ hereby agrees to be bound by the provisions of Sections 6.1, 6.2 and 6.7 of the AZ License to the same extent as PB is."},{"id":"p0642","text":"10.5 Confidential Status of the Agreement. Subject to Section 10.2 and Section 10.6, the terms of this Agreement, including the form of Program Transfer Agreement (whether or not executed by the Parties), are deemed to be Confidential Information and will be subject to the confidentiality requirements of this ARTICLE 10, with each Party being deemed a Receiving Party for such purposes. The Parties each acknowledge that it will be necessary for PB to file this Agreement with the US Securities and Exchange Commission and to make other required public disclosures regarding the terms of this Agreement, and accordingly PB shall prepare a confidential treatment request in connection with such filing and provide SFJ a reasonable opportunity to review and comment on such filing as well as on such other required public disclosures and thereafter use Commercially Reasonable Efforts to obtain confidential treatment as to the terms of this Agreement."},{"id":"p0643","text":"10.6 Publicity. The Parties recognize that following the Effective Date the Parties (either individually or jointly) shall issue mutually agreed press release(s) announcing the execution of this Agreement, and thereafter each Party may from time to time desire to issue additional press releases and make other public statements or disclosures regarding the subject matter of this Agreement, and hereby agree that such additional press releases, public statements and disclosures regarding the terms of this Agreement will be permitted only with the other Party's written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed). Any publication, news release or other public announcement relating to the terms of this Agreement will first be reviewed and approved in writing by both Parties; provided, however, that any disclosure of the minimum information which is required by Applicable Law (including the rules of a securities exchange), as reasonably advised by the disclosing Party's counsel, may be made without the prior consent of the other Party, although the other Party will be given prompt notice of any such legally required disclosure and to the extent practicable will be provided an opportunity to comment on the proposed disclosure and the disclosing Party will consider in"},{"id":"p0644","text":"good faith any comments provided by the other Party on such proposed disclosure. For avoidance of doubt, this Section 10.6 shall not restrict PB from releasing public statements or disclosures regarding PB's development and Commercialization activities with respect to the Product."},{"id":"p0645","text":"10.7 Use of Name. Unless otherwise expressly permitted herein, PB will obtain the written consent of SFJ (which consent will not unreasonably be withheld, conditioned or delayed) prior to referring to SFJ in any correspondence with any Regulatory Authority or Governmental Authority, except as may be required by Applicable Law. SFJ agrees to be bound by Section 6.3 of the AZ License to the same extent as PB is."}]}

content.text: I have what I need. Section 14.3, together with §11.1.1.4 and §10.3, provides the transition and data-return package.

input.quote: transfer control to PB of any or all Clinical Trials being conducted by or on behalf of SFJ or its Affiliate as of the effective date of termination and (y) continue to conduct such Clinical Trials being conducted by or on behalf of SFJ or an Affiliate as of the effective date of termination for up to [***] to enable such transfer to be completed without interruption of any such Clinical Trial
input.rationale: The Agreement contains a usable post-termination transition and data-return regime running in our favour, so no insert is needed. Section 14.3 (surviving termination per §14.4.3.2) obliges SFJ on any termination to: (i) assign sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results to PB (§14.3.1); (ii) assign all Product Filings and, where not immediately transferable, give PB the benefit of them plus "such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB" (§14.3.2); (iii) deliver true, correct and complete copies of all Product Filings and disclose all previously-undisclosed Research Results within a set period after assignment (§14.3.3); (iv) at PB's sole election, either wind down the Clinical Trials at SFJ's cost or transfer control to PB and continue conducting them for a defined transition period so the transfer occurs without interruption (§14.3.4); and (v) assign all Clinical Trial, CRO and Vendor Agreements and cooperate on notices to Sites, Investigators and CROs (§14.3.5). Section 11.1.1.4 independently vests sole and exclusive ownership of the Trial Data Package in PB upon termination "in accordance with any termination clause or section of this Agreement," and PB holds/jointly maintains the Clinical Trials Database and Master File (§§3.5.3, 3.5.4), so our data is not stranded with SFJ. Section 10.3 handles the deletion leg: on expiry or termination, Confidential Information is returned or destroyed at the Disclosing Party's direction, "with such destruction being certified in writing by an authorized officer of the Receiving Party," subject to sensible survival and one-archival-copy carve-outs. This meets the preferred position (transition assistance, data return, certified deletion) and is not walk-away territory — there is no immediate-deletion or no-return risk. Two points noted but not flagged: the transition and delivery periods are redacted ([***]), so we cannot confirm they match the 6-month/30-day benchmarks, and the transition-assistance leg of §14.3.4(ii) is at PB's cost and expense rather than at then-current rates, which is the customary allocation here given SFJ elects nothing. Section 14.3 applies only if SFJ has not triggered a Program Transfer under §3.20; that alternative path is a separately negotiated funding remedy governed by the Exhibit O Program Transfer Agreement and belongs to the change-of-control/remedies rules rather than this one.

input.rationale: No take-or-pay or minimum purchase commitment is imposed on PB. Our payments to SFJ (Article 6) are consideration for the Trial Data Package and arise only if and when Regulatory Approval is obtained, they scale strictly pro rata to the Development Costs SFJ actually pays or incurs under Section 6.2 (an express true-up, including refunds/adjustments and relief if conditional approval is withdrawn), and PB may extinguish them through the Approval or Change of Control Buy-Out Options in Section 6.7. PB also has an at-will exit under Section 14.2.2 before first Regulatory Approval, so this is not a locked multi-year commitment. Two sub-elements are worth noting but are not material deviations: (i) Section 4.2.3(ii) requires PB's Elected Total Amount to be "no less than $110 million and no more than $120 million", which is a minimum draw of SFJ funding rather than a purchase obligation, and the resulting liability remains success-contingent and proportionate; and (ii) the last sentence of Section 4.2.3 requires PB to spend at least the amount SFJ funds, which operates as a use-of-proceeds/diligence covenant satisfied out of SFJ's own funding, not incremental spend on us. The buy-out and 300% termination economics are addressed under the termination/liquidated damages rules and are not double-flagged here. Overall the structure sits at or above the fallback (usage/success-based fees with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty), so no redline.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent PhaseBio Pharmaceuticals Inc. (PB); counterparty is SFJ Pharmaceuticals X, Ltd. (SFJ).

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.rationale: No take-or-pay or minimum purchase commitment is imposed on PB. Our payments to SFJ (Article 6) are consideration for the Trial Data Package and arise only if and when Regulatory Approval is obtained, they scale strictly pro rata to the Development Costs SFJ actually pays or incurs under Section 6.2 (an express true-up, including refunds/adjustments and relief if conditional approval is withdrawn), and PB may extinguish them through the Approval or Change of Control Buy-Out Options in Section 6.7. PB also has an at-will exit under Section 14.2.2 before first Regulatory Approval, so this is not a locked multi-year commitment. Two sub-elements are worth noting but are not material deviations: (i) Section 4.2.3(ii) requires PB's Elected Total Amount to be "no less than $110 million and no more than $120 million", which is a minimum draw of SFJ funding rather than a purchase obligation, and the resulting liability remains success-contingent and proportionate; and (ii) the last sentence of Section 4.2.3 requires PB to spend at least the amount SFJ funds, which operates as a use-of-proceeds/diligence covenant satisfied out of SFJ's own funding, not incremental spend on us. The buy-out and 300% termination economics are addressed under the termination/liquidated damages rules and are not double-flagged here. Overall the structure sits at or above the fallback (usage/success-based fees with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty), so no redline.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Agreement already delivers what TRANSITION asks for, and it does so in our favour:

- **Transition assistance (§14.3.4):** on any termination, at PB's sole election SFJ must either wind down the Clinical Trials at SFJ's own cost, or transfer control to PB and *keep running* them for a defined period so the handover happens without interruption.
- **Cooperation and contract migration (§§14.3.2, 14.3.5):** assignment of all Product Filings with "such assistance and cooperation as necessary or reasonably requested by PB," plus assignment of Clinical Trial, CRO and Vendor Agreements with good-faith cooperation on Site/Investigator/CRO notices.
- **Data return (§§14.3.1, 14.3.3, 11.1.1.4):** SFJ assigns sole ownership of the Trial Data Package and Research Results, delivers complete copies of all Product Filings and discloses all previously-undisclosed Research Results; PB also holds and jointly maintains the Clinical Trials Database and Master File, so the data is never stranded with SFJ.
- **Certified deletion (§10.3):** Confidential Information is returned or destroyed at the Disclosing Party's direction, with destruction "certified in writing by an authorized officer," subject to standard survival and one-archival-copy carve-outs.

Rule:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
No take-or-pay or minimum purchase commitment is imposed on PB. Our payments to SFJ (Article 6) are consideration for the Trial Data Package and arise only if and when Regulatory Approval is obtained, they scale strictly pro rata to the Development Costs SFJ actually pays or incurs under Section 6.2 (an express true-up, including refunds/adjustments and relief if conditional approval is withdrawn), and PB may extinguish them through the Approval or Change of Control Buy-Out Options in Section 6.7. PB also has an at-will exit under Section 14.2.2 before first Regulatory Approval, so this is not a locked multi-year commitment. Two sub-elements are worth noting but are not material deviations: (i) Section 4.2.3(ii) requires PB's Elected Total Amount to be "no less than $110 million and no more than $120 million", which is a minimum draw of SFJ funding rather than a purchase obligation, and the resulting liability remains success-contingent and proportionate; and (ii) the last sentence of Section 4.2.3 requires PB to spend at least the amount SFJ funds, which operates as a use-of-proceeds/diligence covenant satisfied out of SFJ's own funding, not incremental spend on us. The buy-out and 300% termination economics are addressed under the termination/liquidated damages rules and are not double-flagged here. Overall the structure sits at or above the fallback (usage/success-based fees with a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty), so no redline.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

[{"id":"f-indemn-8533a25b","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE","rationale":"Article 12.1 contains a two-way indemnity with proper procedure (notice, control of defence, cooperation, settlement consent), so SFJ does indemnify us for its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, material breach, Protocol breach and AZ License breach. However, the third-party IP infringement risk runs only one way: SFJ's indemnity in 12.1.1 contains no IP element, while our indemnity in 12.1.2(f) covers infringement \"by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder\" — i.e. we indemnify SFJ even for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance, subject only to a gross negligence/wilful misconduct/material breach carve-out. Article 11.3.2 confirms there is no counterparty IP indemnity elsewhere. That fails the fallback (counterparty IP indemnity absent; customer indemnity not narrow) under the detection guidance. The minimal fix keeps our indemnity for the Product and our own performance (appropriate since PB owns and supplies the Product) and adds a mirror SFJ IP indemnity for SFJ's own activities.","proposal":"Add SFJ IP-infringement indemnity for SFJ's own activities and narrow PB's IP indemnity so it no longer covers SFJ's performance","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-1c9a02e8","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"needs_review","rationale":"Worker failed and requires manual review: Tool loop exceeded 12 iterations","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-assign-d2064c79","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"TERM AND TERMINATION","rationale":"Section 15.6 itself is at or above the preferred position: it is mutual, lets PB assign without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, stock sale or asset sale (including reverse triangular mergers), and additionally bars SFJ from assigning to a pharma/biotech competitor without PB's sole-discretion consent. The Affiliate/successor guarantee requirements in p0816 and the encumbrance covenants in 7.5.3 are ordinary financing protections, not an assignment gate, and Section 6.7.2's Change of Control Buy-Out is PB's option (benefits us). The failure is Section 14.2.6: it gives SFJ a sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement following a Change of Control of PB, plus a 150% of Development Costs payment — squarely the playbook's walk-away (a Vendor right to terminate or re-price on Customer's change of control), and it undercuts the M&A carve-out granted in 15.6. Redline deletes SFJ's termination right and the associated payment while keeping PB's notice obligation.","proposal":"Delete SFJ's right to terminate on a PB Change of Control (and the related 150% payment), retaining PB's notice obligation.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-9169297c","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 3.9 IDMC","rationale":"The only exclusivity covenant in the Agreement is Section 3.19, which binds SFJ (and its Affiliates) not to develop or sell Competing Products during the defined Exclusive Period (Section 1.1.68) — an exclusivity granted in our favour, which the rule expressly treats as acceptable. There is no \"sole supplier\", requirements-purchase, or non-procurement obligation on PB: searches for sole supplier / requirements / procure-from-third-party language return nothing, and no mirror-image PB exclusivity commitment exists. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Co-Development and Funding Agreement (Execution Version)

**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — "PB")  
**Re:** Playbook review findings, SFJ co-development / funding agreement  
**Status:** 18 rules assessed — 5 deviations, 11 compliant, 2 requiring manual review

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the execution version against our playbook. The commercial architecture (success-contingent Approval Payments, no minimum purchase, no exclusivity or non-compete on us, no SFJ audit right, and a strong post-termination transition and data-return regime in Article 14.3) sits at or above our preferred positions and needs no redlining.

The exposure is concentrated in the exit and liability provisions. Three items are in walk-away territory: (i) Section 14.2.1's 300% of Development Costs payable by us on SFJ's termination for our breach, expressly "in lieu of any claim for damages" (Section 14.4.2); (ii) Section 14.2.6's SFJ sole-discretion right to terminate on a Change of Control of PB plus a 150% payment, which undercuts the M&A carve-out we obtained in Section 15.6; and (iii) Section 14.2.10's SFJ sole-discretion termination on continued disagreement with a decision we are contractually entitled to make, with Development Costs plus 25% interest. In parallel, our own at-will right in Section 14.2.2 is gated behind $60 million of SFJ spend and closes at first Regulatory Approval, leaving us without a convenience exit for much of a multi-year program.

Two further gaps require attention. Section 15.11 excludes indirect damages but sets **no aggregate monetary cap** for either party, leaving our direct-damages exposure under the broad Article 12 indemnities unlimited. And the Article 12 IP allocation runs one way: SFJ's indemnity at 12.1.1 has no IP element, while ours at 12.1.2(f) covers infringement "by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder" — we indemnify SFJ for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance. Article 11.3.2 confirms no counterparty IP indemnity sits elsewhere. Separately, SFJ performs real services (global CRO oversight and trial execution) with no performance warranty behind them, and the all-caps disclaimer at 13.6.2 carves out only what is "set forth in this Article 13."

Finally, the ownership-of-deliverables (IP) and licence-grant-scope rules did not complete automated review and must be worked manually before we sign off.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | Indemnification and Insurance (12.1.1, 12.1.2(f); cf. 11.3.2) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Needs review** | — (automated review incomplete) |
| 3 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | Term and Termination (14.2.6; cf. 15.6, 6.7.2) |
| 4 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Deviation | Term and Termination (14.2.1; 14.4.2) |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Needs review** | — (automated review incomplete) |
| 6 | High | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | 15.11 (cf. Article 12, 13.6) |
| 7 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | Term and Termination (14.2.2; 14.2.10) |
| 8 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | 3.19 (with 1.1.68) |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | 3.19; Article 7 (7.5.1–7.5.7) |
| 10 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | Representations and Warranties (13.5; 13.6.2; cf. 3.1.4, 3.1.5) |
| 11 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Records (9.1, 9.2; cf. 3.6, 7.6) |
| 12 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | 15.9; 15.10 (15.10.2.2) |
| 13 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | Security Interest (7.4; cf. 7.5.5) |
| 14 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | Development Costs (Article 6, 6.2, 6.7; 4.2.3) |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (fallback) | 15.16 |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | Term and Termination (14.1; 1.1.60) |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | Compliant | Term and Termination (14.3.1–14.3.5; 11.1.1.4; 10.3) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | Indemnification and Insurance (12.3.1–12.3.4) |

### Notes on the deviations and our proposals

- **INDEMN (12.1.1 / 12.1.2(f)):** Add an SFJ IP-infringement indemnity for SFJ's own activities and narrow our IP indemnity so it no longer covers SFJ's performance. We keep our indemnity for the Product and our own performance, which is appropriate since we own and supply the Product.
- **ASSIGN (14.2.6):** Delete SFJ's right to terminate on a PB Change of Control and the related 150% payment, retaining our notice obligation. Section 15.6 is already at or above our preferred position (mutual, Affiliate and successor assignments permitted, including reverse triangular mergers); 14.2.6 undercuts it.
- **LD (14.2.1):** Reduce the 300% multiple to a return of Development Costs actually paid or incurred — the same measure the parties already agreed in Section 14.2.9. We take the fallback here rather than press for no customer-payable amount, given SFJ funds the trials. Related penalty mechanics we would expect to align on the same basis: the 25% interest uplift (14.2.10) and the 150% multiples (14.2.6, 14.2.8.1).
- **LOL-CAP (15.11):** Insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' payments between the parties and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality/data security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and expressly preserving our Article 6 / Section 14.2 payment obligations outside the cap.
- **T4C (14.2.2 / 14.2.10):** Ungate our at-will right (30 days' notice, no $60M spend threshold) and delete SFJ's sole-discretion termination on JSC disagreement with its payment consequence. We accept the 300% exit payment in 14.2.2 as the priced return in this funding bargain rather than press the preferred no-penalty position.
- **WARRANTY (13.5):** Add an SFJ performance warranty for the SFJ Services (workmanlike standard, SFJ SOPs, Protocol, Applicable Law including GCP and ICH) with re-performance at SFJ's cost, excluded from Development Costs. We inserted it into 13.5 so it falls automatically within the 13.6.2 carve-out; no fixed warranty period is proposed because these are continuous trial-conduct obligations.

## Walk-away items

These three provisions are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **Section 14.2.1 (with 14.4.2)** — 300% of all Development Costs paid or incurred, accelerated on SFJ's termination for our material breach and standing "in lieu of any claim for damages," payable regardless of whether Regulatory Approval is ever obtained. This can exceed the value remaining to us under the Agreement.
2. **Section 14.2.6** — SFJ's sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement on a Change of Control of PB, plus a 150% of Development Costs payment. A vendor right to terminate or re-price on our change of control is an express walk-away.
3. **Section 14.2.10** — SFJ's "sole discretion," immediate-notice termination triggered by its continued disagreement with a decision we are contractually entitled to make, with Development Costs plus 25% interest payable by us.

## Next steps

1. **Complete the two open rules.** Manually review ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP) and licence grant scope (LICENSE); automated review failed on both and neither has a verified position. No sign-off until these close.
2. **Issue the redlines** on the five deviations as drafted above, leading with the three walk-away provisions in Article 14 and the Section 15.11 cap.
3. **Confirm the redactions.** Obtain the unredacted figures for: insurance limits under 12.3.2 (against USD 1M/2M CGL and USD 2M E&O); the non-solicit tail period in 15.16 (target 12 months or less from the end of the individual's involvement; revisit anything above 24 months); and the transition and delivery periods in 14.3.3–14.3.4 (against the 6-month/30-day benchmarks).
4. **Confirm position on the Program Transfer path.** Section 14.3 applies only if SFJ has not triggered a Program Transfer under Section 3.20; the Exhibit O Program Transfer Agreement should be reviewed under the change-of-control/remedies rules.
5. **Hold the line on the compliant items.** In particular, resist any SFJ attempt to introduce an audit or inspection right; if one is introduced, we would require it be limited to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at SFJ's cost absent a >5% discrepancy, with no direct access to our systems.
6. **Noted, not flagged (for awareness only):** Delaware law in 15.9 sits at our fallback rather than the preferred New York choice, and 15.10 uses domestic ICDR arbitration (New York seat, FAA-governed) rather than New York County courts. The Section 7.5.5 Licensing Transaction consent gate is a financing covenant we are treating under the negative-covenant rules, not as exclusivity or non-compete. Section 12.3 has no express cyber/privacy liability line.
"}

And the Article 12 IP allocation runs one way: SFJ's indemnity at 12.1.1 has no IP element, while ours at 12.1.2(f) covers infringement "by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder" — we indemnify SFJ for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance. Article 11.3.2 confirms no counterparty IP indemnity sits elsewhere. Separately, SFJ performs real services (global CRO oversight and trial execution) with no performance warranty behind them, and the all-caps disclaimer at 13.6.2 carves out only what is "set forth in this Article 13."

Finally, the ownership-of-deliverables (IP) and licence-grant-scope rules did not complete automated review and must be worked manually before we sign off.

### Notes on the deviations and our proposals

- **INDEMN (12.1.1 / 12.1.2(f)):** Add an SFJ IP-infringement indemnity for SFJ's own activities and narrow our IP indemnity so it no longer covers SFJ's performance. We keep our indemnity for the Product and our own performance, which is appropriate since we own and supply the Product.
- **ASSIGN (14.2.6):** Delete SFJ's right to terminate on a PB Change of Control and the related 150% payment, retaining our notice obligation. Section 15.6 is already at or above our preferred position (mutual, Affiliate and successor assignments permitted, including reverse triangular mergers); 14.2.6 undercuts it.
- **LD (14.2.1):** Reduce the 300% multiple to a return of Development Costs actually paid or incurred — the same measure the parties already agreed in Section 14.2.9. We take the fallback here rather than press for no customer-payable amount, given SFJ funds the trials. Related penalty mechanics we would expect to align on the same basis: the 25% interest uplift (14.2.10) and the 150% multiples (14.2.6, 14.2.8.1).
- **LOL-CAP (15.11):** Insert a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of 12 months' payments between the parties and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality/data security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and expressly preserving our Article 6 / Section 14.2 payment obligations outside the cap.
- **T4C (14.2.2 / 14.2.10):** Ungate our at-will right (30 days' notice, no $60M spend threshold) and delete SFJ's sole-discretion termination on JSC disagreement with its payment consequence. We accept the 300% exit payment in 14.2.2 as the priced return in this funding bargain rather than press the preferred no-penalty position.
- **WARRANTY (13.5):** Add an SFJ performance warranty for the SFJ Services (workmanlike standard, SFJ SOPs, Protocol, Applicable Law including GCP and ICH) with re-performance at SFJ's cost, excluded from Development Costs. We inserted it into 13.5 so it falls automatically within the 13.6.2 carve-out; no fixed warranty period is proposed because these are continuous trial-conduct obligations.

## Walk-away items

These three provisions are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **Section 14.2.1 (with 14.4.2)** — 300% of all Development Costs paid or incurred, accelerated on SFJ's termination for our material breach and standing "in lieu of any claim for damages," payable regardless of whether Regulatory Approval is ever obtained. This can exceed the value remaining to us under the Agreement.
2. **Section 14.2.6** — SFJ's sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement on a Change of Control of PB, plus a 150% of Development Costs payment. A vendor right to terminate or re-price on our change of control is an express walk-away.
3. **Section 14.2.10** — SFJ's "sole discretion," immediate-notice termination triggered by its continued disagreement with a decision we are contractually entitled to make, with Development Costs plus 25% interest payable by us.
